newsitem.title: USA: SEC sues former officers of T2 Medical.
newsitem.headline: SEC sues former officers of T2 Medical.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) sued four officers of T2 Medical Inc, a former publicly traded provider of at home infusion therapy, for financial-fraud and insider trading violations, said a complaint filed by the SEC in the Southern District Court in New York.

T2, which at the time of the alleged fraud was an independent company, later became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Coram Healthcare Corp, which was formed through a merger of T2 and three other publicly-held home infusion companies in July 1994.
A Coram spokesperson said that neither Coram nor its subsidiary, T2, are parties in this suit.

The four former T2 officers were President and Chief Executive Officer Joseph Allegra; Treasurer and Chief Financial Officer David Hersh; Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer J. Lee Ledbetter; and Executive Vice President H. Flynn Clyburn.

The SEC said in its complaint that the officers engaged in a fraudulent accounting scheme by materially overstating T2's fiscal 1993 first quarter net income by approximately $4.0 million and its 1993 second quarter net income by approximately $8.8 million.
The SEC also said that Ledbetter sold T2 common stock based on insider information in June 1993, thereby avoiding substantial losses.

As a result of the fraudulent accounting, the price of the company's common stock fell 51 percent to $6.625 on August 16, 1993 from $13.625 on August 12, 1993, the date of the announcement, said the complaint.
The company restated its net income for the first and second quarters of fiscal 1993 on August 23 of that year.

The SEC seeks injunctive relief against each of the officers, an order imposing monetary penalties on Allegra, Hersh and Ledbetter, an order requiring Ledbetter to disgorge the losses he avoided and an order barring Allegra, Hersh and Ledbetter from serving as officers of any SEC filing company.
